report:
Reviewed the complete fresh crates.sage_ir.types.calls.selected_semantics claim, four implementation entries and three tests. Requirements are selected function identity, dispatch family, owner substitutions, method substitutions, and (for trait methods) Self plus the selected trait reference. The qualification is that proof need not return a concrete impl identity. Captured relevant typed-IR/RFD context and fixture/helper dependencies.

Implementation: tytree::ResolvedCallTarget stores function, dispatch and separate owner/method type-argument slices; StaticTrait carries Self and TraitRef, with no selected impl field. method.rs builds that target for its conservative trait slice after fixed-trait proof classification, using receiver Self and empty method arguments where only owner Self is supported. Broader generic candidates remain unknown rather than being fabricated. Its external inherent path builds Direct targets; instantiation separates owner and method type arguments at the signature's owner generic boundary. operator.rs constructs a StaticTrait target with selected function, left Self, selected trait reference, owner [left,right] substitutions and empty method substitutions for the supported operator signature. finalize.rs copies the selected function unchanged and recursively resolves/copies both argument slices and StaticTrait Self/trait arguments into the completed stash. These four entries support the represented call slices; they do not establish all direct/generic cases.

The ordinary local_operator_impl_can_choose_distinct_rhs_and_output test inspects the actual custom addition completed body. It requires ResolvedCall, selected function name add, exactly two owner substitutions, their nominal names Left and Right, and result type Sum. It requires empty diagnostics and checks the cold query log includes the LocalAdt partition. This is substantive owner-substitution/output evidence; it does not directly assert dispatch or method argument contents. The fixture supplies impl Add<Right> for Left with Output=Sum, so distinct types make the owner assertions meaningful.

The ordinary clone_method_call_is_elaborated_to_a_resolved_trait_call test inspects DbDropGuard::db, requires no diagnostics, a resolved clone call, StaticTrait dispatch with Clone trait reference, ADT Self and a one-argument receiver. It traverses explicit shared reference, resolved field and dereference/local nodes, checks field type equals Self and the field owner name is DbDropGuard. It establishes retained trait identity/Self and actual completed call shape; the ADT pattern does not alone prove Self's symbol name, and the test does not assert owner/method substitution slices. These limits are not inflated into complete substitution coverage.

The TODO types_calls_selected_semantics test contains no assertions and explicitly retains complete direct/static-trait substitution cases and generic trait calls. It is justified by the conservative method implementation and the coverage limits above. Its replacement requires direct tree assertions for owner and nonempty method substitutions, direct/static dispatch, and generic trait calls retaining Self/trait evidence without demanding a concrete selected impl. The absence of an impl field in the schema and use of proof certainty support that qualification architecturally, but the generic behavioral matrix remains deferred.

Helper inspection: source helpers create the actual Sage crate and query its bodies; the twice helper invokes the inspection twice and returns the first result with logs. The proxy helper supplies external metadata from the binary-operator fixture, while Sage computes the body. assert_symbol_name checks actual symbol names. BuiltinDeriveTcx supplies explicit Clone/Sized metadata, clone identity and shared receiver signature for the clone fixture. Assertions remain visible in both annotated tests. No execution or wider test coverage is inferred from helpers or comments.

Validation was source inspection of fresh inputs and captured dependencies. No source edits or behavioral tests were performed; coordinator-run suites are separate execution evidence. No requested edits: the represented call metadata and meaningful partial tests are supported, while the explicit TODO preserves the full direct/generic substitution matrix. No N/A exception or weakened claim is used.
